note: Item codes som_1..som_14 are the .sav column names W1/W2/W3_som_N with the wave prefix stripped by data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_build.py (crosswalk key phq15; no rename, no positional step, no recode or reverse-coding). Variable labels are identical in all three waves for all 14 items ('During the past 7 days, how much have you been bothered by any of the following problems? - <symptom>'); the shared stem went to instructions and the symptom to item_text. The study administered 14 of the 15 PHQ-15 items: the menstrual item (canonical item 4, 'Menstrual cramps or other problems with your periods') is absent; the W1 Qualtrics questionnaire prints row codes (1),(2),(3),(5)..(15) with (4) skipped, and the archive .sav renumbers the remaining rows consecutively, so som_1..som_3 = canonical items 1-3 and som_4..som_14 = canonical items 5-15. This renumbering is identical in W1, W2 and W3 (labels checked per wave), so no code is ambiguous across waves. One deviation from the .sav label: som_11 is labelled 'Constipation, loose bowels, or diarrhoea' in the .sav but reads 'Constipation, loose bowels, or diarrhea' in every questionnaire (W1 p.59, W2, W3 Phase 1 and 2) and in the APA/PHQ-15 source; the questionnaire spelling (what respondents saw) is shipped. All other 13 item_text values equal the .sav labels and questionnaire rows verbatim. option_text = .sav value labels 0=Not bothered at all, 1=Bothered a little, 2=Bothered a lot, identical across waves and items and matching the questionnaire column headers (Qualtrics prints recode values 34-36; the archive .sav and live table carry 0-2). Cross-check (not required for data_labels): .sav per-wave x item x resp counts match the live table cell-for-cell, 126/126 (3 waves x 14 items x 3 levels); live 76300 rows, 2878 ids, wave rows 28350/19684/28266. Wave-1 item means are semantically coherent (som_10 sexual pain 0.104 and som_7 fainting 0.114 lowest; som_13 tired 0.477 and som_14 sleep 0.524 highest). The OSF 'McBride et al. (2020) measures information.docx' describes the scale as the PHQ-15 scored 0-30 (a 15-item range); the .sav's own W{1,2,3}_Somatic_Total is labelled '(14 items)', matching the data. Rights: instrument_rights_register PHQ/GAD family verdict=ship (phqscreeners.com express grant: 'All PHQ, GAD-7 screeners and translations are downloadable from this website and no permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute them.'); the register row is scoped PHQ-2/9 and GAD-2/7 but the clause covers all PHQ screeners, PHQ-15 included; applied, not re-derived, and no register row written. The administered wording is APA's DSM-5 Level 2 adaptation (7-day timeframe); its PDF states 'Rights granted: This measure can be reproduced without permission by researchers and by clinicians for use with their patients.' and 'This measure was adapted from the Patient Health Questionnaire Physical Symptoms (PHQ-15]), which is in the public domain ... To request permission for any other use beyond what is stipulated above, contact: The measure is in the public domain and can be used without permission.' The APA page answers its own 'any other use' question with no reservation, so nothing is reserved. It also carries a fitness caution ('They should be used in research and evaluation as potentially useful tools to enhance clinical decision-making and not as the sole basis for making a clinical diagnosis.'), which disclaims fitness and does not block. English administration.
public_note: The study administered 14 of the 15 PHQ-15 items (the menstrual item was omitted) and numbered them consecutively, so som_4..som_14 correspond to canonical PHQ-15 items 5..15, not items 4..14; the timeframe is the past 7 days (APA DSM-5 Level 2 adaptation) rather than the original PHQ-15's past 4 weeks
